clue.text: Vehicle in which Cabinet position is secured after seat's safe?

definitions.text: Vehicle in which Cabinet position is secured after seat's safe?

parts.words: Cabinet position is secured after seat's safe
parts.note: surface reading: a politician wins a government post once their parliamentary constituency is safe

parts.words: Vehicle in which Cabinet position is secured
parts.note: setter's reading: a cupboard is strapped in place in a removals lorry, loaded after the chair and the strongbox

explanation.surface: A politician's career moves up a gear: a safe seat leads to a Cabinet post.
explanation.walkthrough: Cabinet, seat and safe all look political but are items of household furniture; a safe seat is a constituency a party cannot lose.
explanation.definitionFit: A removals lorry is the large vehicle that carries cupboards, chairs and strongboxes between houses.

clue.text: Joyful Parisian is entertained by quintet

indicators.note: being entertained by a host means sitting inside their house, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a quintet is a group of five
est is French for 'is', as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A cheerful Frenchman is being hosted by a group of five musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: Parisian marks the next word as French: a Parisian says est where an English speaker says is.
explanation.definitionFit: Festive describes a celebratory, merry mood, so it is a synonym of joyful.

clue.text: 20 oboes?
Rest in travel breaks

indicators.note: when something breaks it falls apart, so the letters before it are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Taking a pause partway through a long journey.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval is a pause or break between periods of activity, such as in a play.

clue.text: Escort drug dealer, avoiding leader of posse

indicators.note: avoiding the first letter of posse means that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a pusher is someone who sells illegal drugs

explanation.surface: Someone escorts a dealer away while dodging a sheriff's gang.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher guides or accompanies people to their seats, so as a verb it means to conduct.

clue.text: Peer misses out, ignored by current rulers

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters are rearranged
something ignored is left out, so the letter for current is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: taken as written
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A lord loses out, overlooked by the people in charge today.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I from PEER MISSES, then rearrange the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Empresses are female monarchs who govern empires, so they are rulers.

clue.text: Recognise start of Coldplay record during function

indicators.note: during means within, so the preceding pieces sit inside the word for function

parts.note: to act is to function or operate

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the band's name
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Acknowledging a Coldplay album played at some event.
explanation.walkthrough: AC(C EP)T.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept something is to acknowledge or admit it as valid, which is a sense of recognise.

clue.text: Cabaret star Gwyn perhaps in small car

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the Mini is a famous small British car
Nell Gwyn was a Restoration actress and royal mistress; 'perhaps' marks her as one example of the name

explanation.surface: A cabaret performer called Gwyn crammed into a tiny car.
explanation.walkthrough: MIN(NELL)I.
explanation.definitionFit: Liza Minnelli won an Oscar for the film Cabaret, playing Sally Bowles, so she is literally its star.

clue.text: Hack on northern river

parts.note: to hack something off is to sever it
N is the standard abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: Chopping away at something on a river in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second. The Severn is Britain's longest river, flowing through Wales and England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Severn is an example of a river, the longest in Great Britain.

clue.text: Stifling hot, sews a top, working for exploitative factory

indicators.note: stifling smothers something, so the jumbled letters wrap around the word for hot
working suggests activity and change, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A worker sews garments in suffocating heat at a factory exploiting its staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stifling hot' reads as a description of the factory, but stifling is the containment signal and hot is the single letter H.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweatshop is a workplace where labourers toil for long hours in poor conditions at low pay.

clue.text: Clubs screen lecture

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
to screen something is to hide it from view

explanation.surface: A golf or card club shows a lecture on a screen.
explanation.definitionFit: To lecture someone is to scold or reprimand them at length, which is what chide means as a verb.

clue.text: One who covers winners now and then outside stable

indicators.note: outside means the kept letters go around the word for stable
now and then means occasionally, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
stable in the sense of secure or certain

explanation.surface: A cover story about occasional winners at a racing stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stable' suggests horses beside 'winners', but it is the adjective meaning steady; IN(SURE)R.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurer provides cover against loss, so the company is literally one that covers you.

clue.text: Former lover criticises English sweep

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a critic pans a show by reviewing it harshly
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An ex-partner slates an Englishman's chimney sweep.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweep looks like a person or verb but is a noun for a wide area.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweep can be a broad stretch of land or sea, the same as a wide open expanse.

clue.text: Can't sneer when fighting Gates?

indicators.note: things fighting are thrown about in a brawl, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot mock Bill Gates when they are at war with him.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised Gates suggests the Microsoft founder; the question mark marks it as plain gates, ways in.
explanation.definitionFit: Gates are examples of entrances, the openings through which people go into a place.

clue.text: Be cheeky and give the game away, undermined by defender

parts.note: a captured spy who talks gives away secrets
a back is a defensive player in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A cheeky player blabs the tactics and is let down by a defender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undermined by' is placement in a down clue: the second word sits underneath the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk back is to answer a superior impudently, which is being cheeky.

clue.text: Winger angry over charge

parts.note: cross means annoyed
a bill is a charge for goods or services

explanation.surface: A wide player in football is furious about a penalty awarded against him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' places the first word above the second in a down clue. Winger sounds like a footballer but means anything with wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbill is a finch with crossed mandible tips, and as a bird it is a creature with wings.

clue.text: International abandoned in obvious scheme

indicators.note: something abandoned is left behind, so that letter is removed from the word that follows

parts.note: plain means clear or obvious
I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: An international match given up in a scheme that was clear to all.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a scheme or programme of action worked out in advance.

clue.text: Estate should get you this money upfront for boat journeys

indicators.note: things that journey are moved about, so the letters travel into a new order
upfront points to the front of the word, its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A landed estate ought to pay cash in advance for trips by boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Estate reads as property but is an estate car, the British name for a station wagon; a car is basic transport.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting from one place to another is the phrase for what basic transport does, so an estate car should manage it.

clue.text: Men's armour delivered

indicators.note: a speech is delivered out loud, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: mail is flexible armour of linked metal rings

explanation.surface: A suit of armour for men has been brought to the door.
explanation.walkthrough: Delivered suggests post, the other sense of the sound-alike, which is a nice false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Male is the adjective for things belonging to or typical of men, matching the possessive.

clue.text: Married Frenchwoman's setter biting Sandler?

indicators.note: a mouth biting something closes around it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as me
Adam Sandler is an American comic actor; the question mark marks him as an example of the name

explanation.surface: The crossword setter takes a bite out of the comedian Sandler.
explanation.walkthrough: M(ADAM)E.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame is the French title for a married woman, equivalent to Mrs.

clue.text: Keeping an eye on yobs, essentially waiting

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its middle letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters
waiting at table means serving food

explanation.surface: A waiter keeping watch over some young louts in the restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: A yob is a British word for a rowdy young hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: Observing means watching attentively, which is what keeping an eye on something involves.

clue.text: Ultimately burgeoning Resistance fools informers

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
asses are idiots

explanation.surface: A growing wartime Resistance movement is betrayed by its own idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: A grass is British slang for a police informer, from rhyming slang grasshopper for copper.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, grasses are people who inform on criminals to the police.

clue.text: Caribbean island yoga Botham takes up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading from bottom to top, so backwards
the phrase takes the letters in, holding them within its words

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: The cricketer Ian Botham starts doing yoga on a Caribbean holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Botham is a famous English cricketer; the island is hidden backwards in yoGA BOTham.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is an island in the southern Caribbean, part of Trinidad and Tobago.

clue.text: Suspicious evidence of debts in the wake of backsliding pal

indicators.note: sliding backwards means the word for pal is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a bud, short for buddy, is a friend
IOUs are signed notes acknowledging money owed

explanation.surface: IOUs left behind by a friend who has fallen back into bad habits look fishy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the wake of' means the debts come after the reversed friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubious can mean doubtful or suspect, as in a dubious character, matching suspicious.

clue.text: Seconds before noon, a trainee reporter returns for liqueur

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for seconds
am means ante meridiem, before midday

indicators.note: something that returns goes back the way it came, so these words are read backwards

parts.note: a cub is a novice journalist

explanation.surface: A junior journalist dashes back just before midday to fetch a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Sambuca is an anise-flavoured Italian liqueur, often served with coffee beans.

clue.text: Prison officer and con

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for a jailer
second meaning: to cheat or swindle someone

explanation.surface: A warder and an inmate side by side in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Con sits naturally beside prison officer as a convict, but here it is the verb meaning to swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: Screw is British slang for a jail guard, and to screw someone is to cheat them out of money.

clue.text: Up to Aunty Jill when outsiders go

indicators.note: when the outer letters leave, only the inner ones remain

parts.note: the inner letters
the inner letters

explanation.surface: A trip up to visit Aunty Jill once the strangers have gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Until, as a preposition, means up to a given point in time, as in open until midnight.

clue.text: Major-domo chats drinking coffee

indicators.note: drinking takes something inside, so the answer lies within these words

parts.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A head butler chats over a cup of coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a type of coffee, originally fine beans shipped from the Yemeni port of that name.

clue.text: Rarities at sea will keep heading for The Needles

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within the other
at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: Rare finds at sea heading for The Needles, the chalk stacks off the Isle of Wight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Needles are rocks off the Isle of Wight, so the capital N hides a verb meaning annoys.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to provoke or annoy them, so needles as a verb matches irritates.

clue.text: Nervous feeling when twerp mends shoes for Spooner

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so that swap is applied here

parts.note: a wally is British slang for a silly person, and a cobbler is someone who repairs footwear; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: A nervous shoemaker frets while the idiot repairs footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the W of WALLY and the C of COBBLES to get COLLY WOBBLES.
explanation.definitionFit: The collywobbles is an informal word for an attack of nerves or butterflies in the stomach.
